facts.statement: The genus Nyctosaurus was first described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1876.
facts.quote: authority: Marsh, 1876

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Nyctosaurus gracilis.
facts.quote: type_species: Nyctosaurus gracilis

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus, meaning "night lizard", was a nyctosaurid pterosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now the mid-western United States.
facts.quote: Nyctosaurus (meaning "night lizard") is a genus of nyctosaurid pterosaur from the Late Cretaceous period of what is now the Niobrara Formation of the mid-western United States

facts.statement: During the time Nyctosaurus lived, the region was covered by an extensive shallow sea.
facts.quote: which, during the time Nyctosaurus was alive, was covered in an extensive shallow sea

facts.statement: At least one species of Nyctosaurus possessed an extraordinarily large antler-like cranial crest.
facts.quote: At least one species possessed an extraordinarily large antler-like cranial crest

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Nyctosaurus flew like modern albatrosses, covering long distances while rarely flapping its wings.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that it would have flown similar to modern-day soaring birds such as albatrosses, which consisted of flying very long distances and rarely flapping

facts.statement: The first Nyctosaurus fossils were described in 1876 by Othniel Charles Marsh based on fragmentary material from the Smoky Hill River site in Kansas.
facts.quote: The first Nyctosaurus fossils were described in 1876 by Othniel Charles Marsh, based on fragmentary material, holotype YPM 1178, from the Smoky Hill River site in Kansas

facts.statement: Marsh named the new genus Nyctosaurus, derived from the Greek words for "night" and "lizard".
facts.quote: Marsh reclassified the species in its own genus, which he named Nyctosaurus, derived from the Greek νύξ (nyx, "night") and σαῦρος (sauros, "lizard")

facts.statement: In 1953, Llewellyn Ivor Price named a partial humerus found in Brazil as the species N. lamegoi.
facts.quote: In 1953, Brazilian paleontologist Llewellyn Ivor Price named a partial humerus, DGM 238-R found in Brazil, N. lamegoi

facts.statement: The species N. lamegoi has an estimated wingspan of four metres.
facts.quote: This species has an estimated wingspan of four metres

facts.statement: In 1972, a skeleton discovered in 1962 by George Fryer Sternberg was named N. bonneri.
facts.quote: In 1972, a new skeleton, FHSM VP-2148, in 1962 discovered by George Fryer Sternberg, was named N. bonneri

facts.statement: In the early 2000s, Kenneth Jenkins collected two specimens that were the first to conclusively demonstrate that Nyctosaurus had very large and elaborate crests in mature individuals.
facts.quote: In the early 2000s, Kenneth Jenkins of Ellis, Kansas collected two specimens of Nyctosaurus, which were the first to demonstrate conclusively that not only was this species crested, but that the crest in mature specimens was very large and elaborate

facts.statement: Paleontologist Chris Bennett published a description of the specimens collected by Kenneth Jenkins in 2003.
facts.quote: Bennett published a description of the specimens in 2003

facts.statement: Despite their unusual crests, the specimens collected by Kenneth Jenkins were otherwise indistinguishable from other Nyctosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: Despite the unusual crests, the specimens were otherwise indistinguishable from other specimens of Nyctosaurus

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus had anatomy similar to its close relative and contemporary, Pteranodon.
facts.quote: Nyctosaurus was similar in anatomy to its close relative and contemporary, Pteranodon

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus had relatively long wings that were similar in shape to modern seabirds.
facts.quote: It had relatively long wings, similar in shape to modern seabirds

facts.statement: Some estimates by Peter Wellnhofer in 1991 suggested a total wingspan of about 2.9 meters.
facts.quote: Some wingspan estimates by German paleontologist Peter Wellnhofer in 1991 however, reached a total of about 2.9 m

facts.statement: N. gracilis is estimated to have had a body length of about 37.6 cm, a wingspan of 2.72 m, and a weight of 1.86 kg.
facts.quote: It is estimated that N. gracillis had about 37.6 cm body length, 2.72 m wingspan and 1.86 kg weight

facts.statement: The tips of the jaws were thin and needle sharp.
facts.quote: The jaw tips were thin and needle sharp

facts.statement: The wing structure of Nyctosaurus generally resembles that of the modern-day albatross.
facts.quote: The wing structure generally resembles that of the modern-day albatross, and therefore also flew like it

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus had only three phalanges in its wing fingers, whereas other pterodactyloids typically had four.
facts.quote: Another distinctive feature seen in Nyctosaurus was that it only had three phalanges instead of four, as seen in other pterodactyloids

facts.statement: Scientists conjecture that Nyctosaurus spent almost all its time in the air and rarely landed due to impaired ground movement.
facts.quote: As a result, it was likely to have impaired its movement on the ground, leading scientists to conjecture that it spent almost all of its time on the wing and rarely landed

facts.statement: N. gracilis and N. lamegoi were placed within the family Nyctosauridae as sister taxa to Muzquizopteryx.
facts.quote: Two species of Nyctosaurus (N. gracilis and "N." lamegoi) were included in the analysis, and were placed within the family Nyctosauridae, sister taxa to Muzquizopteryx

facts.statement: In 2018, Nicholas Longrich and colleagues restricted the clade Pteranodontia to only pteranodontids and nyctosaurids.
facts.quote: In 2018, a topology by Nicholas Longrich and colleagues had made the clade Pteranodontoidea the more inclusive group, while Pteranodontia was restricted to only pteranodontids and nyctosaurids

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus grew from hatching to an adult wingspan of over 2 meters in less than a year.
facts.quote: Fully adult specimens are no larger than some immature specimens such as P 25026 (pictured below), indicating that Nyctosaurus went from hatching to adult size (with wingspans of 2 m or more) in under a year.

facts.statement: The large head crest of Nyctosaurus only began to develop after the animal reached one year of age.
facts.quote: Some sub-adult specimens have been preserved with their skulls in nearly pristine condition, and lack any trace of a head crest, indicating that the distinctively large crest only began to develop after the first year of life.

facts.statement: Fully adult, large-crested Nyctosaurus specimens may have lived to be 5 or 10 years old.
facts.quote: These individuals may have been 5 or even 10 years old at the time of their deaths.

facts.statement: Two specimens described in 2003 preserved an enormous double-pronged crest on Nyctosaurus.
facts.quote: Two specimens (KJ1 and KJ2) described in 2003, however, preserved an enormous double-pronged crest.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Christopher Bennett concluded that the crest was likely used solely for display, though other scientists had hypothesized it supported a flight 'headsail'.
facts.quote: Bennett concluded that the crest was most likely used solely for display, citing similar structures in modern animals.

facts.statement: Research suggests the crest was probably not sexually dimorphic, as both sexes of related species like Pteranodon possessed crests.
facts.quote: Bennett also argued that the crest was probably not a sexually dimorphic character, as in most crested pterosaurs, including the related Pteranodon, both sexes are crested and it is only the size and shape of the crest that differs.

facts.statement: Researchers estimated the cruising speed of Nyctosaurus gracilis to be 9.6 meters per second (34.5 km/h or 21.4 mph).
facts.quote: Using these calculations, they estimated the cruising speed of Nyctosaurus gracilis as 9.6 meters/second (34.5 kilometers/hour or 21.4 miles/hour).

facts.statement: All known Nyctosaurus fossils come from the Smoky Hill Chalk of Kansas, part of the Niobrara Formation.
facts.quote: All known Nyctosaurus fossils come from the Smoky Hill Chalk of Kansas, part of the Niobrara Formation.

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus lived between 85 and 84.5 million years ago during a marine regression of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: These limestone deposits were laid down during a marine regression of the Western Interior Seaway that lasted between 85 and 84.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus Nyctosaurus was described by O.C. Marsh in 1876.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Marsh, 1876

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Nyctosaurus is Pteranodon gracilis.
facts.quote: type_species: Pteranodon gracilis

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus was anatomically similar to its close contemporary relative, Pteranodon.
facts.quote: Nyctosaurus era similar anatómicamente a su pariente cercano contemporáneo, Pteranodon.

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus was much smaller than Pteranodon, reaching an adult wingspan of 2 meters and a maximum weight of nearly 1.86 kilograms.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, era mucho menor que Pteranodon, alcanzando una envergadura en la adultez de 2 metros y un peso máximo de cerca de 1.86 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The total body length of Nyctosaurus was 37 centimeters.
facts.quote: La longitud total del cuerpo era de 37 centímetros.

facts.statement: Some specimens preserve a distinctive crest at least 55 centimeters high in older individuals, which is nearly three times the length of the head.
facts.quote: Algunos especímenes preservan una cresta distintiva, de al menos 55 centímetros de alto en los especímenes de mayor edad, relativamente gigantesca comparada con el resto del cuerpo y cerca de tres veces mayor que la longitud de la cabeza.

facts.statement: The upward-pointing crest prong was at least 42 centimeters long, while the backward-pointing prong measured at least 32 centimeters.
facts.quote: La vara que apuntaba hacia arriba era de al menos 42 centímetros de largo y la que apunta hacia atrás mide al menos 32 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The jaws of Nyctosaurus were long and extremely pointed.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas de Nyctosaurus eran largas y extremadamente puntiagudas.

facts.statement: The jaw tips were thin and sharp like a pin, often broken in fossils to make one jaw appear longer, though they were likely equal in length in life.
facts.quote: Las puntas de las mandíbulas eran delgadas y aguzadas como un alfiler, y frecuentemente se encuentran rotas en los especímenes fósiles, dando la apariencia de que una mandíbula es más larga que la otra, aunque en vida era probablemente iguales en longitud.

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus reached adult size with wingspans of 2 meters or more in less than one year.
facts.quote: Nyctosaurus alcanzaba el tamaño adulto (con envergaduras de 2 metros o más) en menos de un año.

facts.statement: Adult Nyctosaurus individuals may have lived to be 5 to 10 years old before dying.
facts.quote: Estos individuos pueden haber tenido 5 o incluso 10 años de edad al momento de sus muertes.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Christopher Bennett concluded that the crest was likely used only for display, citing similar structures in modern animals.
facts.quote: Bennett concluyó que probablemente la cresta era usada solo como forma de exhibición, citando estructuras similares en los animales modernos.

facts.statement: Christopher Bennett argued that the crest was not a sexual dimorphism trait, suggesting both sexes had crests that differed in shape and size.
facts.quote: Bennett también argumentó que la cresta no era una característica de dimorfismo sexual, como en muchos pterosaurios crestados, incluyendo a su pariente Pteranodon, sino que ambos sexos eran crestados aunque la forma y tamaño de la cresta diferían.

facts.statement: Calculations by Sankar Chatterjee and R.J. Templin estimated the cruising speed of Nyctosaurus gracilis at 9.6 meters per second (34.5 kilometers per hour).
facts.quote: Usando estos cálculos, llegaron a la conclusión de que la velocidad de crucero de Nyctosaurus gracilis era de 9.6 metros/segundo (equivalentes a 34.5 kilómetros por hora).

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus fossils were deposited in the Smoky Hill Limestone between 85 and 84.5 million years ago during a marine regression of the Niobrara Sea.
facts.quote: Estos depósitos de calizas fueron depositados durante una regresión marina del Mar de Niobrara que se produjo entre 85 y 84.5 millones de años.

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus existed for a short duration between 88 and 80.5 million years ago, unlike its relative Pteranodon which spanned a longer range.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, Nyctosaurus fue un género de escasa duración, a diferencia de su pariente Pteranodon, el cual es encontrado a través de casi todos los estratos de Niobrara hasta la sobrepuesta Formación Pierre Shale, y existió entre hace 88 a 80.5 millones de años.

facts.statement: In 1902, Samuel Wendell Williston described the most complete skeleton known at the time (P 25026), which was discovered in 1901 by H. T. Martin.
facts.quote: En 1902, Samuel Wendell Williston describió el esqueleto más completo hasta entonces conocido (P 25026) descubierto en 1901 por H. T. Martin.

facts.statement: In the early 2000s, Kenneth Jenkins discovered two specimens that conclusively demonstrated that adult Nyctosaurus had very large and elaborate crests.
facts.quote: A principios de la década de 2000, Kenneth Jenkins de Ellis, Kansas encontró dos especímens de Nyctosaurus los cuales fueron los primeros en demostrar de manera concluyente que no solo esta especie era crestada, sino que la cresta de los especímenes adultos era muy grande y elaborada.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Chris Bennett published a description of the crest-bearing specimens in 2003.
facts.quote: Bennett publicó una descripción de los ejemplares en 2003.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh incorrectly changed the genus name to Nyctodactylus in 1881, which remains its modern synonym.
facts.quote: En 1881, Marsh asumió incorrectamente que el nombre ya había sido usado y lo cambió a Nyctodactylus, el cual es desde entonces su sinónimo más moderno.

facts.statement: In 1953, Llewellyn Ivor Price named a partial humerus found in Brazil as N. lamegoi, honoring geologist Alberto Ribeiro Lamego.
facts.quote: En 1953, Llewellyn Ivor Price nombró a un húmero parcial, DMGM 258-R hallado en Brasil, N. lamegoi; el nombre de la especie es en honor del geólogo Alberto Ribeiro Lamego.

facts.statement: A skeleton discovered in 1962 by George Fryer Sternberg was named N. bonneri in 1972 but is now considered a synonym of N. gracilis.
facts.quote: En 1972 un nuevo esqueleto, FHSM VP-2148, descubierto en 1962 por George Fryer Sternberg, fue nombrado N. bonneri; este es considerado como un sinónimo de N. gracilis.

facts.statement: Robert Milton Schoch renamed Pteranodon nanus to Nyctosaurus nanus in 1984, though the validity of this species is currently under scrutiny.
facts.quote: En 1984 Robert Milton Schoch renombró a Pteranodon nanus (Marsh 1881), una forma "enana" del género, Nyctosaurus nanus. La cuestión de si esta especie es válida está actualmente pendiente de escrutinio adicional.

facts.statement: According to Andres and Myers (2013), Nyctosaurus is phylogenetically situated within the group Pteranodontia.
facts.quote: A continuación se muestra un cladograma con la situación filogenética de este género dentro de Pteranodontia según Andres y Myers (2013).

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus belongs to the parent group Pterodactyloidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Pterodactyloidea

facts.statement: Nyctosaurus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Nyctosaurus as the Albian to Maastrichtian stages (110.1 to 66 million years ago).
